LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE WORD CLASSES: PRONOUNS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words replace names of people or things in sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication
2. use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE WORD CLASSES: PRONOUNS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE WORD CLASSES: PRONOUNS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression

What this means
In this part you learn to use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns to a partner. (skill: use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication.
3. Practise this skill: use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words replace names of people or things in sentences?
2. Which words do we use to show that something belongs to us?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use Word classes: Pronouns means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify personal and possessive pronouns used as subjects and objects for communication.
5. Be able to: use personal and possessive pronouns as subject and object correctly for self- expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
